# Repository guidance for agents

This repository owns the Android emulator plugin. Preserve concurrent user work
and inspect the current branch, remote state and applicable instructions before
editing. Keep unrelated worktrees and unreleased feature branches out of a release.

## Source and generated files

- Edit shared code under `runtime/`; `plugins/android-emulator-plugin/runtime/`
  is generated by `npm run build` and committed for installation.
- The same build copies root screenshots and the authoritative root LICENSE and
  NOTICE into the installable bundle. Rebuild rather than hand-editing those copies.
- Keep the top-level license and third-party licenses intact. Update the inventory
  and notices for changes to binaries, downloads, copied code or shipped artwork.

## Required changelog and release process

Read [GITHUB-RELEASES.md](GITHUB-RELEASES.md) before preparing a version or release.
Maintain [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) as part of the change, with a nonempty section
matching the plugin/runtime version. Packaging checks this automatically.

- Ground entries in actual commits since the previous release tag. Classify added
  features, changed behavior, fixes and breaking changes; give migration and new
  requirements when relevant. Never invent release dates or events.
- Historical development versions must be labelled as development history, not
  retroactively described as published releases. Use this repository's evidence;
  importing history from another repository requires substantiated provenance.
- Commit the complete source and generated bundle, then run the documented local
  packaging command. It builds, runs tests, inspects the ZIP and emits checksums,
  provenance, review gaps and release notes from the matching changelog section.
- Keep the source commit, existing version tag, ZIP, report and published notes
  aligned. Inspect licensing and artifact contents before publication. Verify the
  remote source/tag, downloadable asset bytes and GitHub-visible CI state afterward.
- Build and test locally by default. Do not dispatch Actions or introduce automatic
  push, PR, tag, release or scheduled CI triggers. Do not change repository settings
  or credentials to bypass this rule. A manual CI run needs explicit authorization.
- Pushes, tags and releases require the user's request or established authorization;
  use authorization already supplied in the task. Prepare a reviewable result first.
  GitHub release publication does not authorize OpenAI Registry submission, policy
  attestations, new legal agreements or unsupported host compatibility claims.

The manual workflow is optional infrastructure. Local packaging and publication
remain fully supported without GitHub Actions credits.
